name: news_headlines
description: Retrieves the latest real-time news headlines and article summaries from BBC News and The Guardian across multiple topic categories. Use this tool when an agent needs current news about a specific topic, wants to summarise today's headlines, needs to research recent events, monitor a subject area for new developments, or build a news briefing. Supports filtering by topic category (technology, business, science, health, politics, sport, AI, world, general) and optional keyword search within results. Returns structured articles with headline, description, source name, article URL, and publication date — sorted by most recent first. No API key required. Data sourced directly from BBC News and The Guardian public RSS feeds.

topic.description: News topic category to retrieve headlines for. Accepted values: 'general' (top stories across all categories), 'technology' (tech industry and digital news), 'business' (markets, economy, and corporate news), 'science' (research, environment, and discoveries), 'health' (medical and public health news), 'politics' (government and political news), 'sport' (sports and athletics), 'ai' (artificial intelligence and machine learning news), 'world' (international and global news). Defaults to 'general' if not specified or if an unrecognised value is provided.

keyword.description: Optional search keyword to filter headlines. Only articles whose title or description contains this keyword will be returned. Case-insensitive. Example: 'OpenAI', 'interest rates', 'climate change'. Leave empty to return all headlines for the chosen topic.

limit.description: Maximum number of articles to return. Defaults to 10. Minimum 1, maximum 20. Use a lower number for a quick briefing and a higher number for comprehensive coverage.

topic.description: The topic category that was queried

keyword.description: The keyword filter that was applied, or null if none

articles.description: List of news articles sorted by publication date descending (most recent first)

url.description: Direct link to the full article

source.description: Name of the news source (BBC News or The Guardian)

fetched_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when headlines were fetched

sources.description: List of RSS feed sources consulted
